chip: Les usines chinoises partout dans le monde
title: 15. Les entreprises chinoises construisent des usines partout dans le monde
gist: Chinese companies have spent over $200bn building factories abroad in the last three years, spreading into nearly every region and pulling their suppliers along with them, especially in EVs, solar power and AI hardware. Weak demand at home, US tariffs, and generous incentives from countries like Egypt and Serbia are driving the shift, and Chinese firms are also building the ports and rail lines to connect it all. Trouble spots remain: US tariff threats and new Chinese export controls at home.

body.fr: Les entreprises chinoises {{construisent|are building}} des usines dans le monde entier.

bd.meaning: Chinese companies are building factories all over the world.
bd.key: French present covers English “is/are -ing.” No separate continuous form is needed.

body.fr: En trois ans, elles {{ont dépensé|have spent}} plus de 200 milliards de dollars.

bd.meaning: In three years, they have spent more than 200 billion dollars.
bd.key: avoir + past participle = the past. ont dépensé = “have spent.”

body.fr: Leurs {{fournisseurs|suppliers}} {{les suivent|follow them}} dans les nouveaux pays.

bd.meaning: Their suppliers follow them into the new countries.
bd.key: “les” in front of the verb = “them.” Object pronouns jump before the verb in French, not after like in English.

body.fr: À la maison, la demande est {{faible|weak}} et la concurrence est forte.

bd.meaning: At home, demand is weak and competition is strong.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Les taxes douanières américaines {{poussent|push}} aussi les entreprises {{à partir|to leave}}.

bd.meaning: American tariffs also push companies to leave.
bd.key: pousser qqn à + verb = “push someone to.” The little word à links the two verbs.

body.fr: Des pays comme l'Égypte {{offrent|offer}} de bonnes conditions.

bd.meaning: Countries like Egypt offer good conditions.
bd.key: “bonnes” goes BEFORE the noun, like vrai, grand and petit — a handful of everyday adjectives break the usual “after the noun” rule.

body.fr: En Égypte, une entreprise chinoise construit une {{ferme solaire|solar farm}} géante.

bd.meaning: In Egypt, a Chinese company is building a giant solar farm.
bd.key: “géante” agrees with the noun: feminine ferme takes the feminine ending -e.

body.fr: En Serbie, une usine chinoise {{fabrique|makes}} des pièces pour Volkswagen et Ford.

bd.meaning: In Serbia, a Chinese factory makes parts for Volkswagen and Ford.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Les voitures électriques chinoises sont {{un spectacle courant|a common sight}} {{de Rio à Londres|from Rio to London}}.

bd.meaning: Chinese electric cars are a common sight from Rio to London.
bd.key: “de … à …” = “from … to ….” A simple way to describe a range of places.

body.fr: La Chine {{investit aussi|also invests}} dans des ports {{à l'étranger|abroad}}.

bd.meaning: China also invests in ports abroad.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Elle {{possède ou finance|owns or finances}} plus de 130 ports dans d'autres pays.

bd.meaning: It owns or finances more than 130 ports in other countries.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Mais {{tout ne va pas bien|not everything is going well}}.

bd.meaning: But not everything is going well.
bd.key: aller bien = “to be going well,” a fixed phrase — here wrapped in the ne … pas sandwich.

body.fr: Les États-Unis {{menacent|threaten}} d'augmenter encore les taxes douanières.

bd.meaning: The US threatens to raise tariffs even more.
bd.key: menacer de + verb = “threaten to.” Another verb-plus-little-word-plus-verb chain.

body.fr: Et le gouvernement chinois {{limite|limits}} maintenant les exportations de technologie.

bd.meaning: And the Chinese government now limits technology exports.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: {{Malgré tout|despite everything}}, le monde entier {{continue d'acheter|keeps buying}} des produits chinois.

bd.meaning: Despite everything, the whole world keeps buying Chinese products.
bd.key: continuer de/à + plain verb = “keep doing.” Another helper-plus-plain-verb shape.

grammar.en: Object pronouns go BEFORE the verb in French: les suivent = “follow them,” not “follow-them.”

grammar.fr: Les taxes poussent les entreprises à partir
grammar.en: Verb + à/de + verb is how French chains two actions together: pousser à, menacer de, continuer de all follow this shape.
continuer de + plain verb = “keep doing.” Your fourth helper-plus-plain-verb pattern, alongside pouvoir, devoir and vouloir.

quiz.q: Pourquoi les entreprises chinoises construisent-elles des usines à l'étranger ?
quiz.a: Parce que la demande est faible en Chine et les taxes américaines sont élevées. (Because demand is weak in China and American tariffs are high.)

flag: I compressed many country examples from the article (Morocco, Thailand, Hungary, Vietnam) down to two (Egypt, Serbia) to keep the story concrete rather than a list. un spectacle courant is my plain rendering of “a common sight” — a native speaker might more naturally say on en voit partout (“you see them everywhere”), which I avoided here because it needs the pronoun en, not yet introduced at this level.
